match.reason: No bank point matches this Year 7-8 Victorian card: the closest, bus-target-market, is a Year 11-12 Business Management card that also covers market size and trends, and bus-identifying-target-markets is a Year 12 NSW card covering mass, segment and niche marketing, so both are at a clearly different depth and broader than this point.

draft.title: Target markets
card: A target market is the group of customers a business aims to sell to. A business cannot suit everyone, so it picks the people most likely to buy.
A target market can be described by age, income, location and interests. For example, a skate shop might aim at teenagers who live near a skate park.
Knowing its target market helps a business decide what to sell, what price to charge and how to tell people about it.
Customers outside the target market can still buy. The business just does not build its plan around them.
draft.remember: A target market is the group a business chooses to aim at, described by things like age, income, location and interests.

a.q: Which of these best describes a target market?
opts: The group of customers a business aims to sell to
Every person who lives in the same suburb as the business
The customers who have bought from the business before
The other businesses that sell similar products
a.why: A target market is the group a business chooses to aim at. Past customers are not the same thing, because a business may aim at people who have never bought from it yet.
a.clue: Think about who the business plans around.

b.q: Mia opens a café in Dubbo that sells cheap breakfasts and quick coffees near a university campus. Which description is most likely her target market?
opts: University students who live or study nearby
Retired people who live in another town
Business owners who want expensive dinners
Tourists who visit only in the summer holidays
b.why: Cheap food, quick service and a spot near a campus suit students who live or study nearby. The other groups differ in location, income or interests from what Mia's café offers.
b.clue: Match the price, the place and the product to the customers.

a.best: The group of customers a business aims to sell to

b.best: University students who live or study nearby
